identification: Rough-sawn live-edge Tasmanian timber slab, about 2 m long, wide, with ripple/fiddleback figure, a reddish heart streak and a small burl/birdseye cluster at the top. Catalogued as Huon pine; species not provable from photo (pale yellow, tight rings fits, but reddish streak and ripple could also be blackwood, myrtle or celery top). Sits in a row of near-identical lots 1117 to 1119, so one of a group of slabs sold by Gowans from the same source.

viewing_check: Smell a fresh cut or sanded patch (Huon pine has a strong, sweet, oily scent) and photograph the end grain: very fine, even growth rings, pale yellow; reddish streak may mean myrtle or blackwood instead. Measure length, width and thickness (thin 25 mm slabs are worth far less than 50 mm), and check for cracks, splits, borer holes and how deep the top-end void runs.
